historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr and the FY2027 guidance, decelerating toward a 3% terminal rate; equity CAGR is not meaningful (structurally negative book equity from debt-funded buybacks) so revenue/EPS CAGRs are the anchors instead of the house equity-CAGR rule
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Owner-FCF CAGR (3yr -6.5%, 5yr -10.1%) is NEGATIVE while revenue (+5.2%/+6.8%) and EPS (+4.9%/+9.9%) grew. The gap is capex rising from 4.3% of revenue (FY2021) to 7.05% (FY2026) on the Mega Hub, store and technology build, plus an EBITDA margin that has slipped from 22.9% to 21.7% and working capital absorbing cash as AP/inventory falls -- not a collapse in demand. EPS growth is partly mechanical (buybacks against roughly flat net income: $2,528M FY2023, $2,573M FY2026), so EPS CAGR is not the growth anchor either.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs end at FY2026 (FY2023 and FY2021 starts). Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - interest income; the FY2021 start point is not stripped of interest income (not in the extracted filings; ~$5M, <0.1pp on the CAGR). FY2021 was the pandemic-peak FCF year, which flatters neither end fairly -- the 5yr figure overstates the structural decline.

scenario_narratives.base: Guided operating trajectory plays out: DIY flat-to-soft, commercial compounding on the Mega Hub buildout, capex normalizing from its current cyclical peak back toward AZO's historical ~5% of revenue as the buildout genuinely nears completion, tariff pressure persistent but managed.
scenario_narratives.bull: Commercial execution and Mega Hub payback beat guidance, tariff mitigation expands margin, capex cycle peaks and normalizes earlier, unlocking FCF sooner.
scenario_narratives.bear: Consumer-driven DIY decline, tariff escalation outpaces mitigation, capex stays elevated longer than guided, and the debt-funded capital structure becomes a binding constraint as FCF tightens.

valuation_philosophy.summary: AutoZone is a mature, non-discretionary auto-parts retailer/distributor whose FCF generation has been temporarily depressed by a multi-year capex supercycle (Mega Hub network buildout, international expansion, technology investment) that management has signaled is nearing completion. The negative shareholders' equity is a deliberate, decades-long financial-engineering choice (debt-funded buybacks against consistently strong operating cash flow), not a sign of distress -- it is valued here on enterprise cash flow and normalized for capex reverting toward historical levels, not on book equity.
key_risks_to_valuation: Zero balance-sheet cushion: if FCF deteriorates from a recession or margin compression, there is no equity buffer -- leverage risk is real, not just optical

Capex has not started normalising: FY2026 was 7.05% of revenue and FY2027 is guided higher; the taper to ~5% is management's framing, not yet an observed fact, and it is worth roughly a fifth of base value
EBITDA margin has fallen three years running (23.5% -> 22.3% -> 21.7%) and the FY2026 figure leaned on a non-repeating $96M tariff refund; the base case assumes the decline stops in FY2027
CFO Jamere Jackson leaves 2026-11-25 with no successor named, ahead of the Q1 FY2027 print (2026-12-08) and the refinancing of $600M notes due June 2027 plus $1.0B commercial paper
DIY softness could deepen with a broader consumer pullback, only partially offset by commercial/DIFM growth

inputs.sbc_source: AZO FY2026 10-K cash-flow statement, 'Share-based compensation expense' add-back $136.804M (AZO_Annual_FY2026.txt:2372); same basis as the prior build. The statement of stockholders' deficit shows $142.8M credited to APIC for FY2026; no separate equity-award tax-withholding line is disclosed, so the cash-flow add-back is used as-is and nothing is summed on top.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: last Saturday in August (52/53-week fiscal year)
inputs.wacc_rationale: CAPM on MARKET-value capital weights (book equity is negative from decades of debt-funded buybacks, so book D/E is meaningless): rf 4.2% (10yr UST proxy), ERP 5.0%, beta 0.85 (non-discretionary retail demand but financial leverage lifts beta above unlevered peers); pretax cost of debt ~5.3% (recent AZO senior notes coupons), after-tax ~4.2% at 21% cash tax; weights from market cap ~$45.8B / total debt ~$9.0B (~84%/16%) -> WACC ~7.75%, rounded to 8.0% base with a leverage-risk margin given the zero-equity-cushion capital structure. Bull 7.5% (spread tightens as commercial mix improves credit profile), Bear 9.5% (leverage risk repriced in a downturn / higher-for-longer rates) UPDATE 2026-11-19: UNCHANGED at 8.3/7.5/9.5 (base stays at the 8.3% set in the prior sanity-check pass). Re-derived on current weights (market cap ~$54.8B / debt $9.08B, ~86%/14%) the CAPM figure is ~7.8%, inside the existing margin. The CFO resignation and the FY2027 refinancing ($600M 3.750% notes due June 2027 plus $1.0B commercial paper, both classified long-term against $2.2B of undrawn revolver) are not charged in the discount rate: refinancing/leverage risk is already carried by the 20% bear weight, and adding a WACC premium on top would charge it twice.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (ASC 842): rent is an opex line inside EBITDA and the $3.67B operating lease liability is NOT in net debt -- charged once, in the flows. Finance leases: $417.3M of liabilities at 2026-08-29 ($114.9M current in accrued expenses + $302.5M in other long-term liabilities, AZO_Annual_FY2026.txt:2848-2851) sit OUTSIDE the balance-sheet 'Long-term debt' line, and their $109.0M/yr principal repayment is a financing outflow that the EBITDA-based flows never see. The prior build described them as inside total debt; they are not, so they were charged nowhere. They are now deducted once, in equity_bridge.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- AZO has no reported noncontrolling interests.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF (component build), unchanged from the 2026-09-26 build -- standard US operating retailer/distributor; the negative book equity (stockholders' deficit) is a deliberate debt-funded buyback structure (adjusted debt/EBITDAR 2.5x in FY2025 and FY2026), not distress. No MEMORY.md entry exists for AZO; the model matches the prior valuation. UPDATE 2026-11-19 -- what changed: (1) FY0 ROLLED FY2025 -> FY2026 now that the FY2026 10-K (FYE 2026-08-29, signed 2026-10-26) is filed: base revenue $20,338.6M, owner FCF $1,666.0M = reported FCF $1,815.5M (OCF $3,249.1M - capex $1,433.6M) - SBC $136.8M - interest income $12.7M. Every driver path was shifted one year left so each value stays attached to the fiscal year it was judged for; year 10 (FY2036) repeats the old terminal value. (2) Anchors refreshed: net debt $8,752.2M (debt $9,078.3M, cash $326.1M) and 16.557M diluted shares, both at 2026-08-29. (3) Finance leases ($417.3M) added to the equity bridge -- a method correction, see lease_treatment. (4) EBITDA margin re-judged, base and bull: FY2026 actual was 21.67% (operating profit $3,723.3M + D&A $684.3M) against the 22.0% modelled, and that 21.67% includes $96.0M of non-repeating IEEPA tariff refunds (ex-refund ~21.2%) net of a $128.0M non-cash LIFO charge. Margin has now fallen three years running (23.5% FY2024, 22.3% FY2025, 21.7% FY2026). The base path restarts at 21.8% in FY2027 and climbs at the old slope, i.e. the recovery slips one year; the 23.0% mature level is unchanged. Bull likewise slips one year from a 22.4% start (25.0% mature level unchanged). Bear already sat below the actual and is only shifted. (5) Capex re-judged for the guidance year: FY2026 actual was 7.05% of revenue (below the 7.3% modelled), but FY2027 is guided UP -- the 10-K says investment will 'slightly increase' and the Q4 call figure recorded in Analysis.json is ~$1.65B (~7.65% of base-case FY2027 revenue). The prior path had FY2027 at 6.8%, below guidance. Base FY2027 is now 7.4% (~$1.60B, between the two readings), bull 7.1%, bear 7.8%, and the taper to 5.0/4.0/5.7% slips one year behind it; the peak is FY2027, not FY2026. LEFT UNCHANGED, deliberately: growth paths (FY2026 actual +7.4% vs 7.0% modelled, with ~1.3pp from FX; base FY2027 6.0% is consistent with guidance of flat-to-low-single-digit domestic comps, high-single to low-double-digit commercial growth and ~400 new stores on 8,031 -- would move on Q1 FY2027 comps on 2026-12-08 breaking out of the guided range); SBC % path (actual 0.67% vs 0.72% modelled, left slightly conservative; would move if grants reprice with a new CFO/management package); D&A % (actual 3.36% vs 3.4%); cash tax path (cash taxes paid were only $312M against a $678M provision because of deferred taxes and tax-credit investments -- the model's ~21% on EBIT is deliberately the normal rate, not the sheltered one); wc_capture 3% (AP/inventory slid again, 114.2% -> 111.1%, and inventory absorbed $833M, but the scalar is worth ~$40M/yr; would turn negative if AP/inventory falls toward 100%); WACC, terminal growth and cap multiples; scenario weights 20/50/30. The CFO departure (Jamere Jackson to FedEx, effective 2026-11-25, external search, no successor) moves no driver by itself: he leaves for a larger role, FY2027 guidance predates the resignation and has not been withdrawn. It would move the bear weight or WACC if a successor changed the 2.5x adjusted-debt/EBITDAR target or the buyback policy, or if the June 2027 refinancing priced materially wide of the ~5% recent coupons. 10-year horizon retained: the owner-FCF margin is still normalising past year 5 as capex tapers. Interest income ($12.7M) is immaterial and the company is in net debt; the standard strip is applied for formula consistency. House and street sit close together because SBC is <1% of revenue. The prior DCF JSON's current_price had been price-refreshed after its valuation date; reconciliation.prior_version.price_then is the price the prior Drivers file was built at. The base-case terminal cap of 16x and WACC of 8.3% set in the 2026-09-26 sanity-check pass are carried unchanged.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at the balance-sheet date: 16.173M shares outstanding at 2026-08-29 (FY2026 10-K balance sheet) + 0.384M dilutive stock equivalents (FY2026 EPS table) = 16.557M. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The 10-K cover count is 16.094M at 2026-10-19 after a further 106,862 shares bought for $310.6M; that later count is deliberately NOT used because the cash that bought those shares is not in the 2026-08-29 net debt -- pairing the October count with the August balance sheet would count the buyback's benefit without its cost. Replaces the prior build's extrapolated 16.6M.
inputs.buyback_note: Repurchaser: FY2026 treasury purchases $2,013.2M cash (579k shares; FY2025 $1,578.2M, FY2024 $3,140.9M), a further $310.6M from 2026-08-30 to 2026-10-19, $1.3B authorization remaining. Buybacks are ~1.2x owner FCF and are part-funded by debt (net debt +$224M in FY2026), so the flat-count convention is more than funded; they are value-neutral in this model.

bear.narrative: DIY softness deepens into an outright multi-year decline as a broader consumer pullback (recession) hits discretionary vehicle maintenance spend, and commercial growth decelerates toward mid-single-digits as the Mega Hub buildout's easiest gains are already captured. Tariff escalation is not offset by vendor renegotiation fast enough, compressing gross margin structurally (no repeat of one-off refunds, and LIFO charges keep running above $80M/quarter). Capex stays elevated for longer than management's 'nearing completion' framing because store growth continues chasing growth that is not materializing, delaying the FCF margin recovery. The zero-equity-cushion, debt-funded capital structure becomes a real constraint: WACC rises on refinancing-cost and leverage-risk repricing, and buyback pace slows as free cash flow tightens, removing the mechanical EPS tailwind investors have relied on for a decade. Update 2026-11-19: capex stays at 7.8% in FY2027 with the taper one year later; a prolonged CFO vacancy through the June 2027 refinancing is part of this path, not a separate charge.

base.narrative: Management's FY2027 guide plays out: domestic comps flat-to-low-single-digit with DIY soft, commercial compounding high-single to low-double-digit off the Mega Hub network (172 hubs toward ~300 within three years), ~400 new stores, international at a slower Brazil pace. EBITDA margin starts from the FY2026 actual stripped of most of the tariff-refund benefit (21.8% vs 21.67% reported and ~21.2% ex-refund, with the non-cash LIFO drag fading) and recovers to 23.0% -- still below FY2024's 23.5%. Capex peaks in FY2027 at ~7.4% of revenue as guided, then tapers toward the historical ~5% as the hub and technology build completes. The $96M IEEPA refund is not extrapolated.

bull.narrative: Commercial/DIFM execution closes the gap with O'Reilly faster than guided as the Mega Hub network matures ahead of schedule, driving sustained double-digit commercial growth and margin expansion (mix shift to higher-margin commercial plus operating leverage as the store/Mega Hub capex cycle peaks earlier than management's own timeline). Tariff mitigation (vendor renegotiation, alternate sourcing, pricing) more than offsets cost pressure, expanding gross margin. Capex normalizes faster than base case as the Mega Hub buildout genuinely nears completion by year 3-4, releasing FCF sooner. Aging vehicle fleet tailwind (record 12.8-13.0yr average age) proves more durable and DIY stabilizes rather than continuing to soften. Update 2026-11-19: the margin path starts from 22.4% in FY2027 (FY2026 actual 21.67%) and reaches the same 25.0% one year later than previously modelled; capex peaks at 7.1% in FY2027.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight set slightly above the 15% house default (20%) because the capital structure genuinely has zero book-equity cushion -- a scenario where FCF deteriorates for several years simultaneously with a higher-for-longer rate environment is a real, non-diversifiable risk unique to AZO's decades-long leverage strategy, even though current coverage (~7.5x interest cover) is comfortable today. Bull kept at 30% (below the 35% default) because it requires several things to go right together (faster Mega Hub payback, margin expansion, AND an earlier capex taper) rather than a single lever. UPDATE 2026-11-19: weights unchanged at 20/50/30. The CFO resignation and the FY2027 refinancing are the kind of leverage-structure risk the 20% bear weight already carries; neither is evidence of deteriorating cash flow, and the refinancing is backstopped by $2.2B of undrawn revolver.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
